text: CHAPTER 33
speaker: Narrator

text: The Price of Retention
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The scratching did not return.
speaker: Narrator

text: Something else answered in its place.
speaker: Narrator

text: From inside Balag's pack the fourth knock still hung in the air, unanswered. No one moved to open the straps. Balag had gone still in the particular way he did when the ground itself had become untrustworthy. Enhedu watched the canvas without reaching for it, the figurine turning once in her fingers and then forgotten. Ninsun stood two feet from them, hands clenched white at her sides, and neither of the others looked at her.
speaker: Narrator

text: They were not looking through her.
speaker: Narrator

text: They were looking past her entirely, the way a person's eyes slide off a shadow that has not quite decided whether it wants to be noticed.
speaker: Narrator

text: We need to move,
speaker: Balag

text: Balag said. He stood and slung the pack over one shoulder. The leather straps groaned under the weight of whatever still moved inside it.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Zik? You coming, or are you going to keep staring at your book?
speaker: Balag

text: Zik looked from Balag to Ninsun.
speaker: Narrator

text: She was visibly terrified and just as visibly refusing to stop existing because the world around her had decided she was an inconvenience to be filed away.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she whispered. Her voice hitched on his name.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: They don't hear me. It's like I'm not even making sound.
speaker: Ninsun

text: He took a slow breath. His hand drifted to the journal, then past it. He had told himself he would not bargain with the City again. He knew exactly what it cost—the holes it punched cleanly through history, the strange smooth empty spaces that remained afterward like scars with nothing underneath them. The worst part had never been the clean forgetting. It was knowing that something important had been taken and having no shape left behind to mourn.
speaker: Narrator

text: Looking at Ninsun changed the arithmetic.
speaker: Narrator

text: The shadows in the room seemed to curl toward her. The stone behind her had begun to soften at the edges, the way limestone softened when the ledger was preparing to close an account.
speaker: Narrator

text: He spoke without raising his voice.
speaker: Narrator

text: Her name is Ninsun. She is with us. She stays.
speaker: Zik

text: For a moment nothing answered.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then Balag blinked, once, hard, as if something behind his eyes had been forcibly rethreaded. He looked at Ninsun with the startled recognition of a man who has just remembered a debt he did not know he owed.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun,
speaker: Balag

text: he said. The name arrived incomplete, as though retrieved from a damaged tablet.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Right. The scholar.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu's gaze slid toward her and held. Not with warmth. With the remote attention she now gave anything that had been declared relevant by someone else.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun exhaled a sound that was almost a sob and almost nothing.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik felt the cost arrive a heartbeat later.
speaker: Narrator

text: It was not dramatic. A single clean absence opened somewhere behind his ribs—the specific reason he had decided she was worth the price. He still knew her name. He still knew she belonged with them. He still knew he had paid something irreversible to keep her present in the others' minds.
speaker: Narrator

text: He simply could no longer remember what had made her worth that price in the first place.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag shifted the pack on his shoulder. Whatever was inside it had gone quiet.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What did you just do, Zik? Why is she still here?
speaker: Balag

text: Zik looked at her, then at the wall of names behind them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Because I decided she was.
speaker: Zik

text: He was not entirely sure, even as he said it, whether he believed his own answer.
speaker: Narrator

text: They began walking. Ninsun stayed close enough behind him that he could hear the rhythm of her breathing. He knew her name. He knew she belonged with them.
speaker: Narrator

text: The rest was gone.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind them the chisel began again, unhurried and precise.
speaker: Narrator

text: The City kept its records.
speaker: Narrator
